brenton.name: Brenton’s English Septuagint (1851)
brenton.note: Sir Lancelot Brenton’s English translation of the Septuagint (1851), public domain, from eBible.org; the KJV Apocrypha does not include this book. Its verse numbers follow the Greek; its verse 1 begins with the psalm’s heading.

brenton.1:1: This Psalm is a genuine one of David, though supernumerary, composed when he fought in single combat with Goliad. I was small among my brethren, and youngest in my father's house: I tended my father's sheep.
brenton.1:2: My hands formed a musical instrument, and my fingers tuned a psaltery.
brenton.1:3: And who shall tell my Lord? the Lord himself, he himself hears.
brenton.1:4: He sent forth his angel, and took me from my father's sheep, and he anointed me with the oil of his anointing.
brenton.1:5: My brothers were handsome and tall; but the Lord did not take pleasure in them.
brenton.1:6: I went forth to meet the Philistine; and he cursed me by his idols.
brenton.1:7: But I drew his own sword, and beheaded him, and removed reproach from the children of Israel.
